tagline: Small composable skills: grill → spec → tickets → TDD, no framework.
bestFor: Engineers who want discipline without a framework
keyFeatures: User-invoked flow: /grill-with-docs (interview) → /to-spec → /to-tickets (tracer-bullet slices with blocking edges) → /implement (drives /tdd, closes with /code-review)
Shared domain language: grilling maintains a CONTEXT.md glossary and ADRs inline, so specs, tickets, and code use the same terms
Specs and tickets publish to the project's issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, or local Markdown), configured once per repo by /setup-matt-pocock-skills
/wayfinder charts work larger than one session as a map issue of decision tickets, resolved one at a time
Two-axis /code-review (repo standards + spec fidelity) run as parallel sub-agents
Claude Code plugin in the official marketplace; `npx skills` installs editable copies for Codex and other agents
MIT, ~268K stars; explicitly positioned against process-owning frameworks (GSD, BMAD, Spec-Kit)
limitations: A skill collection, not a framework: nothing enforces the flow, and each step is invoked by hand
Specs are consumed through tickets — no maintained living spec in the repo
No worktree isolation or parallel multi-agent orchestration
Depends on an issue tracker for specs, tickets, and wayfinder maps (local Markdown is the fallback)
Single-maintainer project; skill contents change often between releases
